name: Traralgon
bio_draft: Regional town and service hub of Central Gippsland, in the Latrobe Valley.

facts.claim: Largest city in the City of Latrobe, in the east of the Latrobe Valley, Gippsland
Urban population of 26,907 at the 2021 census

access_note: Evidence shows it is a regional service town with no named visitor draw; marginal under COVERAGE (town is a spot only when a draw). Owner/judge to review.
unresolved: visitlatrobe.com.au fetch failed; no visitor-source draw found

name: Old Gippstown
bio_draft: Relocated pioneer township at Moe with historic buildings, machinery and Gippsland's settler history.

facts.claim: Open-air museum and reconstructed pioneer township in Moe, Victoria
Located at 211 Lloyd Street, Moe
Open Wednesday to Sunday

access_note: Open Wed-Sun only; cafe temporarily closed from 24 Aug 2026

name: Walhalla
bio_draft: Restored gold-mining town in a steep valley, with historic buildings and a heritage railway.

facts.claim: Gold-mining town founded in late 1862, home to about 4,000 at its peak and about 20 permanent residents now
Long Tunnel Extended Gold Mine runs underground tours; adult $25 (excl. GST)
Walhalla Goldfields Railway, cemetery, post office museum and ghost tours are listed attractions
Walhalla Historic Area is a Parks Victoria-managed area

access_note: Town is free to wander; mine tour (adult $25, tour basis) is an extra, not the spot price. Parks Victoria page lists no entry fee but not explicitly confirmed.

name: Baw Baw National Park
bio_draft: Alpine plateau park of snow gums, bogs and granite tors, with walks and a ski resort at Mount Baw Baw.

facts.claim: About 13,530 ha national park on the Victorian Alps/Gippsland boundary, about 120 km east of Melbourne
Covers much of the Baw Baw Plateau with snowgum forest and wildflowers in spring
Mushroom Rocks is a maze of giant granite tors on the Australian Alps Walking Track
Mount St Gwinear is a free-entry snow-play area in winter

access_note: Victorian national parks charge no entry; page shows no fee. Consider costBasis 'park' with free:true per owner convention.

name: Mount Baw Baw
bio_draft: Victoria's closest alpine ski resort to Melbourne, also a summit base for summer walks on the Baw Baw plateau.

facts.claim: Alpine resort village at 1450 m amongst snow gum forest on the Baw Baw Plateau
Melbourne's closest ski and snow resort
Summer activities include hiking, mountain biking and walks
Summit on the Baw-Baw Plateau, Great Dividing Range, Gippsland

access_note: Resort entry free in green season; a winter resort entry fee probably applies (not found on page). Facilities closed in green season.
unresolved: winter resort entry fee not found

name: Toorongo Falls
bio_draft: A rainforest waterfall with a short walk beside the Toorongo River near Noojee, shared with the nearby Amphitheatre.

facts.claim: Reserve protects Toorongo Falls and Amphitheatre Falls, about 6 km north-east of Noojee
Walk passes through tall, wet forest with several viewpoints of the falls and continues to Amphitheatre Falls
Main falls about 25 m high, with a viewing platform

name: Tarra-Bulga National Park
bio_draft: Cool-temperate rainforest park of mountain ash and tree ferns, with short walks from Balook.

facts.claim: Small national park in South Gippsland, about 240 km south-east of Melbourne, 33 km south of Traralgon and 24 km north of Yarram
Cool-temperate rainforest of mountain ash, tree ferns and ancient myrtle beech with short fern-lined creek walks
Home to Corrigan's Suspension Bridge through the canopy; the Lyrebird Ridge track starts at the Visitor Centre and its first 300 m is accessible
Jointly managed with the Gunaikurnai people

access_note: Parks Victoria page flags 'additional visitor advice / reported issues / closed' banners in its template; check conditions before visiting
unresolved: Parks Victoria page lists no entry fee and its fees page 404'd; free entry is inferred from the brief's rule for Victorian national parks

name: Corrigan's Suspension Bridge
bio_draft: A suspension bridge walk through rainforest canopy and tree ferns in Tarra-Bulga National Park.

facts.claim: A suspension bridge through the rainforest canopy in Tarra-Bulga National Park with views down into the fern gully
Walk-in site: no dogs, camping, bikes or fires; limbs may fall so take care

unresolved: Parks Victoria site page lists no fee; free inferred as part of a Victorian national park (open site within it); no Wikipedia article

name: Port Albert
bio_draft: Victoria's first port, with a maritime museum, 19th-century buildings and a heritage walk.

facts.claim: Town on Corner Inlet in South Gippsland, 236 km south-east of Melbourne and 13 km south of Yarram
One of the earliest ports established in Victoria; the first settlers arrived in 1841
Port Albert Maritime Museum is at 78 Tarraville Rd

unresolved: museum entry price not fetched (extra inside the town, not the spot's price)

name: Snowy River National Park
bio_draft: Remote gorge and river park with rafting, bushwalking and bush camping.

facts.claim: Large national park in East Gippsland and the Alpine region, about 390 km north-east of Melbourne, covering over 114,000 ha
The Snowy River cuts through Tulloch Ard Gorge; scenery of deep gorges, old growth Alpine Ash and cypress pine woodland
Walks include Little River Gorge, Raymond Creek Falls and Silver Mine; MacKillops Bridge (built 1935) is the canoe launch and river access
Remote area with hot summer days in the northern valley

access_note: MacKillops Bridge had weekday closures for repair works (7am-5pm Mon-Fri); check Parks Victoria for current status
unresolved: Parks Victoria page lists no entry fee and its fees page 404'd; free entry is inferred from the brief's rule for Victorian national parks

name: Errinundra National Park
bio_draft: Plateau park of cool-temperate rainforest and old growth, with a boardwalk and lookout.

facts.claim: National park of 26,875 ha on the Errinundra Plateau in East Gippsland, 373 km east of Melbourne
Cool-temperate rainforest and old growth forest on a high plateau
Visitor sites include the Errinundra Rainforest Boardwalk, Ocean View Lookout and Mt Ellery walking track
Camping areas at Frosty Hollow and Delegate River

access_note: Plateau roads can close in wet weather; check Parks Victoria conditions
unresolved: Parks Victoria page lists no entry fee and its fees page 404'd; free entry is inferred from the brief's rule for Victorian national parks

name: Buchan Caves
bio_draft: Limestone caves with guided tours, a spring-fed swimming pool and a reserve of bushland.

facts.claim: Limestone caves including Royal Cave and Fairy Cave, 3-4 km total length with six entrances, south-west of Buchan in East Gippsland
Victoria's largest cave system; a guided tour is the only way to see it, choose Fairy Cave, Royal Cave or both
Royal Cave has calcite-rimmed pools and Fairy Cave elaborate stalactites and stalagmites; constant 17 C inside
Reserve has walking tracks, campground and kangaroos around the visitor centre

access_note: Tickets must be bought 24 hours in advance online or at the visitor centre; tours are the only way in
unresolved: booking page shows two adult prices ($26.60 and $27.30, likely different periods) with no label for one cave vs both; both-caves price not captured

name: Cape Conran Coastal Park
bio_draft: Coastal park of rock pools, beaches, an East Cape boardwalk and camping on Bass Strait.

facts.claim: Coastal park on Victoria's far-east Wilderness Coast, near Marlo in East Gippsland, about 420 km east of Melbourne
Wild ocean beaches for beachcombing, with whales migrating past from May to October
East Cape Boardwalk has interpretive signs on the Aboriginal history of the Cape
Yeerung Gorge has deep rock pools fed by the East Yeerung River; Banksia Bluff is the main campground

name: Mitchell River National Park
bio_draft: Gorge and river park with the Billy Goat Bluff and Den of Nargun walks near Dargo.

facts.claim: Jointly managed park in Gippsland on Brabralung Country, significant to Gunaikurnai Traditional Owners
Rainforest gully walk to the Den of Nargun, with a loop to the Mitchell River for summer swimming and a lookout
Billy Goat Bend has a lookout over the Mitchell River Gorge and rapids, with picnic tables and camping
Mitchell River Walking Track links Angusvale and the Den of Nargun; the river has Grade III-IV whitewater, best July to December

unresolved: Wikipedia exact title for the Victorian park not fetched (the summary for 'Mitchell River National Park' is a disambiguation page)

name: Den of Nargun
bio_draft: A cultural loop walk to a cave behind a waterfall, the site of an Aboriginal legend, in Mitchell River National Park.

facts.claim: Cave behind a waterfall in a rainforest gully of Mitchell River National Park, reached by a loop walk from a picnic area
Tradition says the Nargun, a being half human and half stone, lives there; Gunaikurnai people and Parks Victoria ask visitors not to enter the cave
The loop continues to Deadcock Den, where Eastern Water Dragons sun themselves, and a lookout over the loop and park, with river access for a swim in warmer months

access_note: The Parks Victoria site page carries a generic 'This area is closed' banner label (template text, unclear if current); check closures before visiting.

facts.claim: Open-air museum in Golden Point, Ballarat, depicting the first ten years after gold was discovered there in 1851
Visitors can pan for real gold, wander an 1850s township and go on an underground mine tour
More than twenty experiences are included in general admission, with live characters and craft workshops

name: Museum of Australian Democracy at Eureka

facts.claim: Interpretive centre in Eureka Stockade Memorial Park with a permanent exhibition on the Eureka Rebellion
Home of the Eureka Flag, which is on display there
Includes a gift shop (free to enter) and a cafe

access_note: The museum 'MADE' closed in 2018 and the site reopened under City of Ballarat as the Eureka Centre; the spot's name should be 'Eureka Centre' (wiki title 'Eureka Centre').
unresolved: Name change recommended: Museum of Australian Democracy at Eureka is now the Eureka Centre

name: Eureka Stockade

facts.claim: Eureka Stockade Memorial Park in Ballarat is considered the site of the 1854 Eureka Stockade rebellion
The park has significant trees, interpretive plaques and monuments honouring those involved
The Battle of the Eureka Stockade was fought on 3 December 1854; the official toll was 27 deaths

access_note: Heavy overlap with ballarat-2 (same park); consider merging.

name: Art Gallery of Ballarat

facts.claim: Oldest regional art gallery in Australia, founded in 1884
Housed in an 1890 building on Lydiard Street North
Free entry since 2008

access_note: Main building at 40 Lydiard St Nth is closed for building upgrades; exhibitions are at Backspace Gallery, 43 Mair St (official site, 2026-11-02).

facts.claim: Shallow artificial urban lake beside the suburb of Wendouree in Ballarat
Name comes from a local Aboriginal word wendaaree, meaning 'go away'
Heritage trams of the Ballarat Tramway Museum run along its shore

name: Ballarat Botanical Gardens

facts.claim: 40-hectare reserve on the western shore of Lake Wendouree
Three zones: a central Victorian 'gardenesque' garden flanked by North and South Gardens
Celebrated its 150th anniversary in 2007

unresolved: council page for the gardens not located; free entry from Wikipedia silence only, unverified

name: Ballarat Wildlife Park

facts.claim: Zoo opened in February 1985 on 10 hectares
Holds over 300 animals including over 100 free-roaming kangaroos
Large reptile collection; hand-feeding kangaroos and koalas offered

access_note: Adult $42 at the gate; online price lower (~$37.80).

name: Kryal Castle

facts.claim: Replica medieval castle 8 km east of Ballarat at Leigh Creek, in the foothills of Mount Warrenheip
Has welcomed visitors since 1974
Offers overnight stays in castle rooms, cabins and tiny homes

unresolved: homepage says "Tickets from only $31.50"; adult general-admission price not confirmed on a tickets page (buy-tickets URL 404)

name: Ballarat Tramway Museum

facts.claim: Volunteer-run operating tramway museum
Heritage trams run on part of the original horse tramway around Lake Wendouree and the Botanical Gardens
Trams ran across Ballarat from 1887 until 1971; the museum holds an archive of 3,500+ items

access_note: Runs on weekends and public holidays (per official site); adult $15.
